checks.note: CoachRegistrationService.verifyPhone and verifyEmail do perform an unguarded read-check-then-write of verificationStatus (load at findOneById, write at setVerificationStatus/save with no lock or re-check), so the lost-update window exists in this file — but the finding's consequence depends on User.java lacking @Version and on AccountSuspensionEventListener committing verificationStatus=SUSPENDED concurrently, and neither of those files is shown.

Within this file the claim holds up: registerCoach's try/catch (lines 101-105) wraps a plain userRepository.save(user) with no flush-triggering operation before method end, and the in-file AC10 comment in verifyEmail confirms @Tsid ids defer the INSERT to commit-time flush. But settling it requires code not shown: BaseEntity/User (to confirm User.id is app-assigned @Tsid), the schema (user_phone_key unique constraint on phone), and ApiAdvice (the finding's verification caveat — whether commit-time DataIntegrityViolationException is unmapped).

The facade shows the uncaught check-then-insert shape (findUserByEmailOrLogin → persistUser → publishEvent, no catch in registerAccount), but the consequence depends on code not shown: whether UserRegistrationService.createUser handles duplicates, whether the UserRegisteredEvent listener and EmailRegistrationStrategy.notifyNewUser are BEFORE_COMMIT/outbox-bound or plain/@Async (the finding's own verification caveat), and whether the user_login_key constraint/@Tsid-deferred insert exist as described.

In verifyEmail, evt is managed (loaded via findByToken in the same transaction), so emailTokenRepository.save(evt) is a flush-free merge; the version-conflict UPDATE first executes at deleteByUserIdAndUsedFalse, saveAndFlush(otpToken), or commit (phone-otp-not-required path), all outside the try/catch at lines 154-158, so the ObjectOptimisticLockingFailureException catch is unreachable. Assumes standard SimpleJpaRepository.save semantics (no custom flushing override shown).

The trigger is real: AuthService.login (class-level @Transactional) calls loginTokenManager.createLoginToken and CookieUtil.addCookie on the live response before the commit at the proxy boundary, so the lines 113-114 comment misstates the ordering. But the consequence depends on whether ApiAdvice/the servlet error dispatch calls response.reset() before rendering the error — that code is not provided and no file-access tools are available, so the caveat cannot be run.
